title: Effect of five dietary emulsifiers on inflammation, permeability, and the gut microbiome: a placebo-controlled randomized trial
authors: Wellens J, Vanderstappen J, Hoekx S, Vissers E, Luppens M, Van Elst L, et al.
followUp: 2 weeks of emulsifier-free diet, then 4 weeks of supplementation
funder: not stated in an accessible source; the full text could not be read. Registry NCT06552156 names Universitaire Ziekenhuizen KU Leuven as lead sponsor and lists no collaborators.
result: Double-blind; brownies with carboxymethylcellulose, polysorbate 80, carrageenan, soy lecithin, native rice starch or no additive (registry doses: carboxymethylcellulose 2.75 g, carrageenan 375 mg and soy lecithin 3.55 g per day). Faecal short-chain fatty acids were lower with carboxymethylcellulose than placebo; faecal calprotectin, C-reactive protein, serum lipopolysaccharide-binding protein and metabolic markers did not differ from placebo; transcellular permeability rose from baseline with carrageenan (P = 0.04). Cholesterol fell after 2 weeks of the emulsifier-free diet.
